extracted.intended_audience: covered entities (health care providers and State Exchanges), Section 1557 Coordinators, compliance officers, and legal/policy staff responsible for civil rights compliance
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts the regulatory requirements and implementation guidance in the final HHS Section 1557 rule regarding designation of a Section 1557 Coordinator and required Section 1557 policies and procedures for covered entities. Focuses on who must comply, what written policies and grievance/recordkeeping procedures are required, and associated operational guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of Section 1557 Coordinator (15+ employees)
rubrics_metrics.description: Covered entities with 15 or more employees must designate at least one employee to serve as a Section 1557 Coordinator to coordinate efforts to comply with and carry out the covered entity's responsibilities under section 1557 and the part. Covered entities may, as appropriate, assign one or more designees to carry out some of the Coordinator's responsibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A covered entity need not hire a new employee for the role; the Coordinator may serve in other capacities so long as those responsibilities do not create a conflict of interest or prevent effective performance. The Coordinator must retain ultimate oversight for ensuring compliance. Large health systems may customize Coordinator/designee configurations, but each individual covered entity must have either a Coordinator or designee responsible for section 1557 compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinator responsibilities (baseline at §92.7(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The regulatory text enumerates responsibilities for the Section 1557 Coordinator (see §92.7(b)) as a baseline of expected duties to promote effective and efficient implementation of section 1557 and the part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The enumerated responsibilities provide a baseline but allow covered entities flexibility to structure duties among Coordinator(s) and designee(s). Covered entities may assign additional duties beyond those enumerated. The Coordinator is expected to facilitate proactive compliance, support investigations, and serve as a central point of contact for issues like language access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinator impartiality and effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Coordinators are expected to perform their duties impartially; OCR appreciates concerns that Coordinators be sufficiently independent to ensure impartiality and transparency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A covered entity may face noncompliance risk if an investigation reveals its Coordinator did not carry out obligations impartially. OCR declined to require the Coordinator to be independent from the covered entity (i.e., not an employee), but the Coordinator must be qualified to effectively and impartially perform the role. Anti-pattern: appointing a Coordinator who privileges the institution over impartial investigation may undermine compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinator contact information in policies and notices
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies and procedures and notices must provide 'contact information' for the Coordinator; providing the job title rather than an individual's name is sufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact information must include a phone number, email address, and mailing address (a general phone/email/ mailing address may be used). Listing only a name without contact channels is insufficient; listing only a job title without any contact details is also insufficient. This approach reduces burdens of updating names and mitigates harassment concerns while ensuring individuals know how to reach the Coordinator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who counts toward the 15-employee threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: OCR will consider the total number of individuals employed by a covered entity when determining whether it has 15 or more employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes full-time and part-time employees and independent contractors; all employees count regardless of job classification (e.g., clinical vs. clerical). The rule intends to avoid gaming hiring practices to evade the threshold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application to small covered entities (<15 employees)
rubrics_metrics.description: Covered entities with fewer than 15 employees are not required to designate a Coordinator, but may voluntarily designate one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR declined to extend the mandatory Coordinator requirement to all covered entities to avoid undue administrative burdens on small providers. Encouraged practice: small entities may still designate a Coordinator to promote compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordination across multiple covered entities/health systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Large health systems may customize Coordinator and designee structures, but each individual covered entity must have either a Coordinator or designee responsible for section 1557 compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR declined to require a specific ratio (e.g., one Coordinator per 250 employees). Covered entities should ensure Coordinator(s)/designee(s) are positioned to effectively perform duties for each legal entity that is a covered entity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegation and use of existing structures
rubrics_metrics.description: A covered entity may assign Coordinator responsibilities to a group, division, or designee(s), and the Coordinator may work within existing organizational structures that receive and investigate grievances or perform other responsibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provided the covered entity identifies an individual Coordinator who retains ultimate oversight, duties may be delegated. Entities may leverage existing grievance collection points and trained staff to implement Coordinator functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinator role and employment/harassment protections
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule does not apply to employment practices, but employees remain protected against retaliation as provided in §§92.303 and 92.304; covered entities should address harassment of Coordinators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If Coordinator experiences harassment by staff, the covered entity should take appropriate measures. If harassment is based on protected characteristics within EEOC jurisdiction, the Coordinator may file an EEOC charge. OCR also encourages reporting threats to law enforcement (FBI tip line).

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinator training and OCR support
rubrics_metrics.description: OCR commits to serve as a resource and partner and plans to make various resources available to assist Coordinators, including training, factsheets, and checklists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR will provide training for new and updating Coordinators, materials to introduce Section 1557 to staff, and checklists to confirm Coordinator responsibilities. Covered entities should use these resources to improve compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinator review of grievance data (encouraged)
rubrics_metrics.description: OCR highly encourages all Coordinators to review grievance data to identify and address potential and actual discriminatory trends revealed in such data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is encouragement, not a mandate. OCR declined to require collection of specific grievance data points in the Coordinator provision because such details are set forth in §92.8(c)(2). Best practice: analyze grievance trends periodically to identify systemic issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment of written Section 1557 Policies and Procedures (§92.8 general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Covered entities must develop and implement written Section 1557 Policies and Procedures designed to facilitate compliance with the requirements of the part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policies and procedures must include an effective date and be reasonably designed taking into account the covered entity's size, complexity, and type of health programs or activities. OCR expects scope/detail to vary by entity; templates are available as a starting point.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required components of Section 1557 Policies and Procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: At minimum, Section 1557 Policies and Procedures must include: a nondiscrimination policy; grievance procedures (for covered entities employing 15 or more persons); language access procedures; auxiliary aids and services procedures; and procedures for reasonable modifications for individuals with disabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covered entities may combine content with policies required under other civil rights statutes if the combined policies clearly comply with Section 1557 and the part. Entities should tailor procedures to their operational realities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nondiscrimination policy content requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The written nondiscrimination policy must, at minimum, provide the Coordinator's contact information (if applicable) and state that the covered entity is prohibited from unlawfully discriminating on the basis of race, color, national origin (including LEP and primary language), sex (including pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, and sex characteristics), age, or disability; and provide language assistance services and appropriate auxiliary aids and services free of charge when necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy language should clearly inform patients/clients of protected bases and the availability of free language/auxiliary services. Use accessible plain language and include contact channels so individuals can request assistance or file grievances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written grievance procedures for covered entities (15+ employees)
rubrics_metrics.description: Covered entities with 15 or more employees must establish written civil rights grievance procedures for their health programs and activities, including ensuring accessibility to individuals with LEP and individuals with disabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures should be accessible (language access, alternative formats) and clearly describe how to file grievances, timelines, resolution steps, and appeal mechanisms. Entities with fewer than 15 employees are encouraged, but not required, to have a grievance procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grievance record retention (§92.8(c)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: A covered entity must retain records related to grievances alleging discrimination on the basis of race, color, national origin, sex, age, or disability for no less than three (3) years from the date of filing of the grievance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retain sufficiently detailed records to support investigations and compliance reviews, while protecting privacy. OCR sought comment on privacy concerns but maintained the three-year retention requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of complainant identity (§92.8(c)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: A covered entity must keep confidential the identity of an individual who has filed a grievance, except as required by law or to the extent necessary to carry out the purposes of the regulation, including conducting any investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain confidentiality protocols and limit personally identifying information in records, disclosing identity only as legally necessary or to conduct investigations. Consider data minimization and secure storage practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language access procedures (§92.8(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Covered entities must develop and implement written language access procedures to support compliance with requirements to take reasonable steps to provide meaningful access to individuals with LEP in health programs and activities under §92.201.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures should explain how to provide interpreters, translated materials, and other LEP services; when they are provided free of charge; how to assess language needs; and how to document language assistance provision. Entities should consider training staff on identifying LEP needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective communication procedures for individuals with disabilities (§92.8(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Covered entities must develop and implement written procedures to ensure communications with individuals with disabilities are as effective as with individuals without disabilities (per §92.202).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures should address auxiliary aids and services, alternative formats, and staff responsibilities to ensure effective communication in clinical and administrative interactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for reasonable modifications for individuals with disabilities (§92.8(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Covered entities must develop and implement written procedures for making reasonable modifications to policies, practices, or procedures that allow individuals with disabilities equal opportunity to participate in health programs and activities as required under §92.205.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures should describe how to request, evaluate, and implement reasonable modifications, including timelines and documentation. Ensure decisions respect nondiscrimination principles and privacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combining Section 1557 policies with other civil rights policies
rubrics_metrics.description: A covered entity may combine the content of policies and procedures required by §92.8 with any policies and procedures pursuant to other civil rights statutory protections, if they clearly comply with section 1557 and the part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When combining, ensure the combined document clearly addresses all Section 1557 requirements and remains accessible and actionable for staff and the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policies and procedures must be dynamic: review and revision (§92.8(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: A covered entity must review and revise its policies and procedures, as necessary, to ensure they are current and in compliance with section 1557 and the rule; a covered entity may change its policies and procedures at any time provided the changed policies comply with the statute and the part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Update policies when law changes or operations change. Maintain version control and effective dates, and communicate substantive changes to staff and relevant stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: OCR-provided templates and technical assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: OCR has developed Section 1557 Policies and Procedures templates available on OCR's website to assist covered entities in tailoring their own policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Templates are starting points; entities must tailor to their size, complexity, and programs. Large entities may need more detailed/customized policies than the templates provide. Use OCR resources to reduce burden and improve compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility on additional optional procedures (telehealth, service animals, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: OCR declined to require additional specified policies (e.g., service animals, telehealth procedures, assessing bilingual staff competency) at this time, but encourages covered entities to develop such procedures as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entities are encouraged to create telehealth procedures (including pre-appointment screenings, patient training), service animal policies, accessibility for medical diagnostic equipment, and other measures to meet Section 1557 obligations even though not mandated in §92.8.

rubrics_metrics.name: OCR enforcement and compliance review approach
rubrics_metrics.description: OCR will determine covered entity compliance with the Coordinator requirement and Policies and Procedures during complaint investigations and affirmative compliance reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entities should maintain documentation of designation, policies, grievance records, training, and related actions to demonstrate compliance during OCR reviews or investigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public notice of OCR findings (OCR practice)
rubrics_metrics.description: OCR's practice is to notify the public via a press release or posting on its website when a violation has been found or a resolution has been reached; covered entities are encouraged but not required to notify participants, enrollees, and beneficiaries of any finding of discrimination and remedial actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR declined to require recipients/State Exchanges to notify participants of findings/remedial actions since similar federal civil rights regulations do not include such a notice requirement. However, recipients may choose to provide notice; OCR also offers a Civil Rights listserv for public information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary vs. mandatory remedial actions (§92.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: §92.6(b) addresses voluntary actions recipients may take to overcome effects limiting participation (these are voluntary); §92.6(a) mandates remedial actions when there is a finding of prohibited discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR declined requests to convert voluntary language to mandatory, preserving a distinction between encouraged voluntary measures and required corrective actions upon a finding of discrimination.
